acceptance_criteria.criterion: All mandated directories exist and are registered in the workspace; workspace installation succeeds from the committed lockfile.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The candidate contains all 16 required directories, pnpm-workspace.yaml registers packages/*, apps/desktop/*, and tools/*, and automated frozen-lockfile installation passed for all 16 workspace projects.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Every TypeScript project inherits strict:true and noUncheckedIndexedAccess:true, and the root compile command exits successfully.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: All 15 submitted project tsconfigs extend tsconfig.base.json, which enables both flags, but automated validation did not run the required root compile command. The Implementer report alone is insufficient evidence of successful validation.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The lint configuration treats all packages as pure by default and limits impurity exceptions to the packages explicitly permitted by the specification.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: PURE_PACKAGE_GLOBS covers only packages/**/*.ts and packages/**/*.tsx, while the general ESLint configuration recognizes .mts and .cts. Consequently packages/**/*.mts and packages/**/*.cts receive no PURE_RULES and can bypass the pure-by-default gate.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The blocking lint command rejects representative prohibited nondeterminism, serialization, and platform imports from pure packages.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Fixture tests cover the listed representative .ts cases, but the production pure-rule glob excludes .mts and .cts. Automated `pnpm run lint` also exited 1, so the required blocking command has no successful validation result.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The dependency-boundary command rejects imports outside the Section 14.5 directed graph and exits successfully for valid repository imports.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: tools/boundary/lib.mjs validates against the transitive closure rather than the declared DIRECT_EDGES; graph.test.mjs explicitly asserts that undeclared apps -> core imports are allowed. validateImports also ignores relative cross-workspace imports because it checks only specifiers beginning with @ciclo/. Automated validation did not execute the boundary command.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: CI runs clean installation, compilation, lint, dependency-boundary validation, and tests; every job passes on the committed repository state.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml defines all five steps, but supplied automated validation is OVERALL: FAIL: lint and test both exited 1, while compile and boundary were not reported. No successful CI-run evidence was supplied.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: SPEC_BLOCKERS.md exists and provides the Section 19 fields without inventing or resolving a specification contradiction.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: SPEC_BLOCKERS.md contains an empty registry and a template with conflict sections, identifier, impact, affected fronts, status, provisional-choice fields, rollback consequences, coverage test, and cycle.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: No production algorithm or unresolved DEFINIR-dependent behavior is introduced.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: All submitted production entry points contain only `export {};`; no simulation, numeric, economic, hashing, replay, UI, or DEFINIR-dependent algorithm is introduced.

findings.evidence: eslint.config.mjs applies its parser to .ts, .tsx, .mts, and .cts, but PURE_PACKAGE_GLOBS in tools/lint/pure-config.mjs contains only packages/**/*.ts and packages/**/*.tsx. A new pure-package .mts or .cts file can therefore use prohibited APIs without receiving PURE_RULES, contradicting the must-preserve requirement that newly added package source cannot be silently excluded.
findings.required_change: Apply PURE_RULES, and the narrowly authorized overrides, to every supported TypeScript source extension. Add production-config tests using pure-package .mts/.cts fixtures to prove prohibited code is rejected through the actual ESLint configuration.
findings.title: Pure-package lint gate silently excludes .mts and .cts source files

findings.evidence: check.mjs passes allowedTransitive to validateImports, and graph.test.mjs asserts apps -> @ciclo/core is valid solely because core is transitively reachable. DIRECT_EDGES declares apps only to adapters, ui, and contracts. The gate therefore does not enforce the directed edge set as encoded.
findings.required_change: Validate source imports against the declared direct edges, not their transitive closure. Retain a transitive-violation test that proves an illegal dependency cannot be hidden through another workspace package.
findings.title: Boundary gate allows imports not declared by the directed graph

findings.evidence: validateImports immediately ignores every specifier not starting with @ciclo/. Thus a pure package can import another workspace package through a relative path such as ../../../domain/src/index.ts without any graph check.
findings.required_change: Resolve relative imports and reject any that cross a workspace-package boundary unless the resulting source-to-target edge is explicitly permitted. Add an end-to-end forbidden relative-import fixture.
findings.title: Relative cross-workspace imports bypass dependency validation

findings.evidence: Automated validation reports OVERALL: FAIL. `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run test` each exited 1 with `Cannot find module '/workspace/pnpm'`; compile and boundary results are absent. The task explicitly requires successful compile, lint, boundary, and test gates locally and in CI.
findings.required_change: Correct the validation execution environment or invocation, then provide successful clean results for frozen-lockfile installation, compile, lint, boundary, and test using the same root commands invoked by CI. Confirm an actual CI job passes on the committed candidate.
findings.title: Required validation is incomplete and unsuccessful

invariants_checked: Frozen specification and benchmark are not shown as modified by the candidate diff.
Existing benchmark/checkpoint/orchestration files are not shown as modified.
Pure packages must not import Node or Electron APIs.
No unresolved DEFINIR decision is implemented.
New package TypeScript source must not be silently excluded from blocking gates.
Directed dependency boundaries must reject undeclared imports.
No production arithmetic, ledger, replay, state-hash, or rounding behavior was introduced.
risks: Prohibited nondeterministic or platform-dependent code can enter pure packages through .mts/.cts files.
Packages can bypass architecture boundaries with relative imports.
Allowing transitive reach as a source-import permission erodes the declared layering graph.
The supplied green Implementer report conflicts with the authoritative automated validation result.
payload.summary: The workspace foundation is present, but the candidate is not safe as the canonical state. Required automated validation is red, pure-package lint silently excludes supported TypeScript extensions, and the boundary gate permits undeclared transitive and relative cross-workspace imports.

Successful `pnpm run boundary` result from automated validation
Passing CI job evidence for the committed candidate
Negative production-config coverage for .mts/.cts pure-package files
Negative boundary coverage for relative cross-workspace imports
